brief: GS equities color for Oct 6: S&P closed +58bps at 7,818 (MOC $2.8bn to sell), NDX +48bps, R2K -68bps, Dow +49bps on below-average volume; VIX -335bps to 15.01, crude +46bps, 10yr -0.025bps, gold +72bps, DXY -31bps, Bitcoin -22bps. NDX/SPX drifted higher as crude and rates stabilized on a bid to Euro bonds plus Bessent commentary; momentum fell for a second session and R2K lagged. Focus: the Power Up America basket jumped ~450bps after GOOGL headlines renewed AI power-demand focus (CEG +12%); HDD names STX/WDC fell 8-10% on competition concerns that spread to semicap equipment (AMAT, KLAC, LRCX); biotech fell ~350bps on AVBP's 46% clinical-miss drop. Activity was muted (floor score 4/10) but skewed to buy. Bartlett attributes the NDX breakout to three drivers: clean HF positioning (nets near 5-year lows), covering of macro hedges, and dollar concentration into Tech/AI crushing market breadth to its lowest since 2000, even as investors stay worried despite strong AI fundamentals. Derivs: SPX skew crushed further, NDX skew steepened; the GS desk likes VIX call spreads to November, flags asset managers' historically short VIX futures positioning, and keeps liking URA/nuclear upside. SPX implied move into tomorrow: 0.39%.
